kind: interim: all ten E0076 loops have ended; E0074 and E0075 still running
source: Slurm job records in evidence/E0076/ and evidence/E0075/, and the fetched per-step summary.json files in the mirror

cost.note: width-100 figure is E0073 f* 0.65 total CPU-hours over all its steps (including its 50-cycle first step and failed steps), so the ratio is rough; E0070 measured 4.7 to 5.6 for twice the width

loops.cost_ratio_note: Total CPU over all steps run divided by steps run: width 200 52.685/45 = 1.171 CPU-hours, width 100 9.68/55 = 0.176, about 6.7 times. Not like-for-like: width 100 covered a wider Gamma range (2.2 to 4.0 against 2.35 to 3.8) and used a 50-cycle first step and caps of 0.5/2.0 CPU-hours against 2.0/8.0 here.
loops.floor_note: The down-branch stop at Gamma 2.3 is the per-step CPU cap (2.0 CPU-hours, 23 of 25 cycles). Corrected Nov 24 (second run), after the checker: the width-100 floor of 2.2 was also a CPU-cap stop (0.5 CPU-hours at Gamma 2.15; width100_stop_modes). Caps scaled four times, cost per step about seven times (down_leg_cost_ratio), so both lower ends are cost floors and the difference between them says nothing about box size.

end_comparison.floor: not comparable: CPU cap stop at both widths (width 200 at Gamma 2.2 after 23 of 25 cycles, 2.021 CPU-hours against a 2.0 cap; width 100 at 2.1 on its 0.5 cap)
end_comparison.top: one-sided: width 200 had a sphere overlap at Gamma 4.05 (after 24 of 25 cycles completed); width 100 completed 4.05 and 4.1 and stopped on its 2.0 CPU-hour cap at 4.15, so width 200 broke at a Gamma width 100 passed, but where width 100 would have stopped for a physical reason is unknown

slow_step_before_top.note: On the way up, the Gamma 4.0 step at width 200 cost 6.234 CPU-hours, about ten times the 0.574 to 0.639 of the steps from 3.65 to 3.95, and the next step (4.05) ended in a sphere overlap. At width 100 the same f* had its expensive step at 4.1 (1.269 CPU-hours against 0.087 to 0.19 from 3.65 to 4.05), then hit the cap at 4.15. One expensive step just below the top is common at width 100 (f* 0.44 at 4.0, 0.50 at 4.05, 0.65 at 4.0); among the five width-200 baseline loops that reached Gamma 3.7, only f* 0.74 shows one. Per-step cpu_seconds, one seed each.

end_comparison.floor: not comparable, one-sided: width 200 stopped on its 2.0 CPU-hour cap at Gamma 2.4 (23 of 25 cycles, 2.005 CPU-hours), so its floor is 2.45; width 100 completed 2.4 and 2.35 and had a sphere overlap at 2.3 (10 cycles), floor 2.35. The width-100 step at 2.4 cost 0.345 CPU-hours; at the measured down-leg ratio of about 7.5 that is about 2.6 CPU-hours at width 200, above the cap. So width 200 stopped for cost one step above where width 100 would still run, and where width 200 would break is unknown.
end_comparison.top: both widths stopped at Gamma 4.05 after completing 4.0, but for different recorded reasons: width 100 was stopped as frozen time (3 slow episodes, 9 cycles, 0.958 CPU-hours), width 200 hit its 8.0 CPU-hour up-leg cap after 17 of 25 cycles with no slow episode recorded. In both, the cost per cycle jumped at 4.05: width 200 0.471 CPU-hours per cycle against 0.0337 at 4.0 (14.0 times), width 100 0.1064 against 0.00634 (16.8 times). This is the first width-200 top set by the up-leg cap. It is set by one sudden slow-down that the narrow box shows at the same Gamma, not by the general cost ratio between the widths.

width100_stop_modes.note: Every non-completed step of the width-100 baseline loops (E0073), read from ramp.jsonl in A0068. cpu_budget stops on the down leg hit the 0.5 CPU-hour cap; on the up leg the 2.0 CPU-hour cap.

down_leg_cost_ratio.note: CPU-hours of a completed 25-cycle step at width 200 divided by the same step at width 100 (same f*, same Gamma), down leg below Gamma 3.0, both steps completed. Step caps were scaled four times from width 100 (0.5 to 2.0 CPU-hours down, 2.0 to 8.0 up; D0046) while a step costs this many times more, so where both widths stopped on the cap, their floors are cost floors and are not comparable.

up_leg_cost_ratio.note: CPU-hours of a completed 25-cycle step at width 200 divided by the same step at width 100 (same f*, same Gamma), up leg above Gamma 3.0 (after the turn at the floor), both steps completed. Width-100 costs from A0068 ramp.jsonl (cpu_seconds). The up-leg cap was scaled four times (2.0 to 8.0 CPU-hours, D0046), so a top that stops on the cap at either width is a cost limit, not a physical one. Added at the checker's request (review of Nov 24 second run).

width100_cost_jump_near_3_35.note: Checker, Nov 24 third review: the up-leg cost ratio of about 11.4 to 11.5 at f* 0.44 and 0.57 comes from the width-100 cost halving between Gamma 3.3 and 3.4 while the width-200 cost stays smooth, not from width 200 being dearer. f* 0.38 shows the mirror image: the width-100 cost rises 1.7 times between 3.3 and 3.35 (0.095 to 0.160 CPU-hours a step) while width 200 stays smooth (1.080 to 1.044), so the up-leg ratio is 11.3 to 13.1 from 3.05 to 3.3 and 5.3 to 8.7 from 3.35 to 4.0. The width-100 fields (A0068, fields.npz, ring spectrum of the height field, 32 frames a cycle) at f* 0.38 keep the same dominant ring (ring k = 4 in units of 2 pi / L, a wavelength of L/4 = 25 sphere diameters) through 3.25 to 3.4; the share of the height variance in that ring, averaged over the 32 phases, is 0.59, 0.609, 0.669 and 0.663 at Gamma 3.25, 3.3, 3.35 and 3.4. So the cost jump comes with the height variance gathering more into the same ring (0.61 to 0.67 between 3.3 and 3.35), with no change of ring, while the mean height variance rises smoothly (0.80 to 0.84). Whether this is a change of pattern type (for example stripes to squares) cannot be told from a ring spectrum; the width-100 height grids in the same files would show it, and were not looked at this run. One seed, one f*.
width100_cost_jump_near_3_35.source: A0068:main-3d-f0.38/step-057 to step-060 fields.npz (fetched, not kept); width-200 step CPU from the mirrored summary.json files of job 164691
